title: First Glare
summary: Kael enters the Last Drop for shade and water. A scarred patron recognizes him as Varnok before Kael has done anything to invite the comparison; Eva notices the room decide what kind of story he is.

panelPlan.text: Wide interior: hard white daylight cuts around Kael in the swinging doors. The Last Drop is busy but watchful; a scarred patron at a side table goes still while Eva, half-bored at the bar, follows his stare.
The patron stands and says the name before Kael has reached the shade. Kael looks behind himself once, genuinely checking whether the man means someone else.
The patron throws a bottle. Kael ducks just enough; glass bursts against the doorframe. Nobody else in the room looks surprised enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I'm sorry. You've got the wrong man.

directionInline.text: Play the first misidentification as social certainty, not supernatural revelation. Kael is mildly inconvenienced, not haunted. Eva's interest is immediate because the room became more interesting the moment he entered.

title: The Table in Shadow
summary: The patron attacks at close range. Kael ends the fight without escalating it, then asks for water as though the important thing is still the heat; Eva decides he is worth bothering.

panelPlan.text: The patron lunges across the aisle. Kael catches the wrist, turns with the momentum and folds him face-down across an empty table.
Several hands drift toward holsters. Kael releases the man, rights a chair and sits in the darkest available corner rather than claiming the room.
Eva brings a chipped cup of water without being asked twice and sits opposite him instead of leaving it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Good, because I don't have the explanation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: He knew a face. Mine happened to be standing there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I've got enough problems I already understand, I don't much care about ones I don't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Bah. Leave it alone. I didn't mean anything by that.

directionInline.text: Eva should sound entertained by a live puzzle, not like an exposition device. Kael does not perform innocence; he simply refuses to let the accusation define the scene.

title: Too Hot Here
summary: Jessa appears outside with Kael's satchel and announces that the settlement is getting too hot for him. Her casual use of 'we' makes Kael briefly wonder whether she, too, has decided he is someone else.

panelPlan.text: Outside in the hard glare, Jessa leans against the battered rig with Kael's satchel already slung over one shoulder. Eva has followed them to the porch, pretending she has another reason to be there.
Jessa tosses the satchel to Kael and nods toward three locals gathering at the far end of the street.
Kael catches the bag, looks from Jessa to the locals, then back to Jessa at the word 'we.' Jessa is already opening the passenger side.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: It's too hot here for you. We're leaving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Fine. I'm leaving. You can come with me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I haven't decided whether you're helping.

directionInline.text: Jessa reads social escalation, not prophecy. Her 'we' is practical and slightly presumptuous. Kael's suspicion that she may be another mistaken-recognition problem should pass quickly when she behaves like herself.

title: Dead Weight
summary: Before Kael can leave, he sees a man being hanged behind the Last Drop. He cuts him down because the immediate human problem overrides the sensible decision to keep moving; Marcus reads the act as proof that 'Varnok' has returned.

panelPlan.text: Kael rounds the rear corner toward the rig and sees boots thrashing below a loading beam. Marcus and two locals are watching the hanging as public discipline, not a secret murder.
Kael climbs a barrel, supports the man's weight with one shoulder and saws through the rope while Marcus shouts from the porch.
The man collapses coughing into the dirt. Kael loosens the rope from his neck. Marcus approaches with a length of pipe, angry and newly certain.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: You always did have to make trouble, Varnok.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I don't know Varnok. I know this man is choking. Lift his shoulders or step back.

directionInline.text: No heroic tableau. Kael's intervention is practical, almost irritated. Marcus uses the mistaken identity to recruit Kael into an existing local power struggle.

title: Marcus's Story
summary: Marcus tries to force Kael into Varnok's old role: enemy, judge, and excuse for violence. Eva arrives expecting spectacle and instead sees Kael keep returning attention to the injured man.

panelPlan.text: Marcus swings the pipe. Kael steps aside; the blow splinters a fence post. Eva appears at the mouth of the alley, suddenly less amused.
Marcus names old offenses and dares Kael to deny them. Kael kneels beside the hanging man, checks his breathing, and asks Eva for the water she is still carrying.
Eva hands it over. Marcus realizes Kael will not give him the duel he wants, and the watching locals begin looking at Marcus rather than Kael.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: You burned my brother out of this place.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: Look me in the face and say that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I'm looking at him right now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Thanks. Easy. Just wet your mouth.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I know. That's making this harder.

directionInline.text: The scene is about control of attention. Kael wins nothing; he simply refuses Marcus's frame until the community's attention shifts to the real present-tense harm.

title: We're Leaving
summary: Jessa brings the rig around. The hanging has broken Marcus's control of the moment, and Kael leaves before the settlement can decide whether he is Varnok, savior, coward, or something else. Eva climbs aboard without permission.

panelPlan.text: The rig slews into the back lot in a cloud of pale dust. Jessa has the passenger door open before it stops.
Kael braces the rescued man against the porch and puts the cut rope into Marcus's hands. The locals' formation has loosened; one of them brings water without being told.
Kael climbs in. Eva is already on the rear step with her small pack. Jessa sees her in the mirror and gives Kael a look that says this is his problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: You can keep thinking that. It's still my name.

directionInline.text: Let the local story continue after Kael exits; he does not solve the settlement. Eva's attachment should feel opportunistic, adventurous and funny rather than fated.

title: Dust on the Lens
summary: Outside the settlement, Eva reveals the first small inconsistency: the scarred patron was already waiting for 'Varnok' before Kael arrived. Kael dismisses it as rumor; Jessa is more interested in how quickly Eva packed.

panelPlan.text: Long horizontal: the rig crosses hard white ground. The Last Drop shrinks behind them; a half-buried black Sunforge shape stands off the road, used by locals as ordinary shade.
Eva rides on the rear step, pleased with herself. She produces a folded scrap she took from the saloon table: a crude description of a dark-haired man and the words 'Varnok comes through today.'
Kael reads it once and hands it back. Jessa watches him in the mirror. Eva waits for the mystery to become important; Kael looks out at the road.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: He had this before you walked in.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I rescued it from being evidence nobody noticed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: It says Varnok would come through today.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Then whoever wrote it got the name wrong.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: The day is the part I don't like.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't agreeing with you. I was narrowing the problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You had his bag before he agreed to go.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I trust what I've seen him do.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I don't know him well enough for a careless one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I can hear both of you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Do either of you know where we're going?

directionInline.text: Seed the larger pattern without proving conspiracy. The note can plausibly be rumor, a setup, or coincidence. End on the trio forming almost accidentally.
